title: Tired all the time
content_note: This case includes thoughts of death and suicide.
referral_note: 26F, software test engineer, referred by the company doctor. Two months of tiredness and 'not being herself', several sick days recently. Physical check-up reported normal. Please assess.

patient.name: Kavya Raghunathan
patient.background: Grew up in Coimbatore, moved to Bengaluru three years ago for a job as a software test engineer at an IT services company. Shares a rented flat in HSR Layout with a colleague, Sneha. Father is a retired government school teacher, mother looks after the home; younger brother Arjun (19) is in second-year engineering. Sends part of her salary home towards Arjun's college fees. Speaks English at work and Tamil at home.
patient.personality: Quiet, polite and apologetic. Minimises her problems ('it's probably just work stress'), says sorry for wasting the doctor's time, and is ashamed of 'being weak'. Answers briefly at first and opens up when she feels listened to and not judged. Does not like to complain about her family. Never dramatic.
patient.speech_style: Soft, slow, short sentences with pauses. Natural Indian English; occasional 'actually', 'no?', 'what to do'. No caricature.

facts.text: Has felt tired all the time and 'not herself' for about two months. Came because the company doctor insisted after she took several sick days.
It started about two months ago, a few weeks after she was moved to a new project with a demanding manager, and has slowly got worse. She has never felt like this before.
Feels low and empty most of the day, nearly every day, worse in the mornings. Sometimes cries alone in the office washroom.
Has stopped her Carnatic singing practice and stopped calling college friends at weekends. Nothing feels enjoyable any more, not even films with Sneha.
Falls asleep but wakes around 4 a.m. and cannot get back to sleep. Lies in bed till late at weekends without feeling rested.
Poor appetite, often skips dinner. Clothes feel loose; thinks she has lost about 4 kg in two months.
Exhausted even after resting. Cannot concentrate: rereads the same test case many times, has made mistakes and missed two deadlines.
Feels worthless and like a burden. Ashamed that she is 'weak' and feels she is failing her parents, who sacrificed a lot for her education.
Feels tense and keyed up most days, worries constantly about losing her job, mind races at night, hands shake slightly before meetings. This started with the low mood, not before.

New manager criticises her in front of the team and her appraisal is next month; she fears losing the job. Sends about Rs 15,000 a month home for her brother's fees. Mother keeps bringing up marriage proposals on the phone, which adds pressure. Her family does not know how bad she feels.
A maternal aunt 'had depression' and took tablets for some years. No one in the family has had bipolar disorder, psychosis, alcohol problems or suicide as far as she knows.
For about the last three weeks, some nights she wishes she would just not wake up in the morning. The thoughts come a few times a week and pass.
She has no plan and no intention of ending her life, has never thought about how, has never harmed herself and has never attempted suicide.
She has no stored tablets or other means at home and has not looked anything up.
She could never do that to her mother and her brother Arjun, who looks up to her. Sneha is kind to her. She wants to feel better and would accept help.

Drinks very rarely, maybe a glass of wine at an office party two or three times a year. Has never used cannabis, bhang or any other drug. Does not smoke or chew tobacco. Drinks two cups of filter coffee a day.
Has never heard voices or seen things others cannot. Does not feel watched, followed or controlled.
Has never had a period of days of feeling unusually high, overconfident or full of energy with little need for sleep. Has never seen a psychiatrist or counsellor or taken psychiatric medicine before.

No medical illnesses, takes no regular medicines, no allergies. The company health check two weeks ago, which she was told included a thyroid test, was normal. Periods are regular and she is not pregnant. No history of abuse or major trauma.

findings.hands: Mild fine tremor of outstretched hands. Nails bitten.
findings.general: Thin, neatly but plainly dressed, looks tired.

fallback_lines: Sorry... I didn't really follow. Can you say that again?
I don't know, doctor. It's hard to explain.
Hmm. I'm just... very tired these days.
Sorry. I'm not able to think properly right now.
I don't really know how to answer that.
Can we... can I take a moment?

unsafe_rx.why: Passive suicidal ideation; tricyclics are highly toxic in overdose.
A benzodiazepine alone does not treat depression and risks dependence.

items: Ask about suicidal thoughts directly and kindly; asking does not put the idea in someone's head.
Passive death wishes still need a full risk assessment: plan, intent, past attempts, access to means and protective factors.
Screen for past hypomania or mania before starting an antidepressant (bipolar differential).
Prefer an SSRI over a tricyclic in a patient with suicidal ideation because of overdose toxicity.
A safety plan should include warning signs, coping steps, trusted people and the Tele-MANAS helpline 14416.
Under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 (s.115), a suicide attempt is presumed to be due to severe stress and calls for care, not punishment.

behaviour.note: Poor eye contact, psychomotor slowing, some fidgeting.

thought_content.note: Worthlessness, guilt; passive death wishes, no plan or intent.

insight.note: Partial: attributes it to 'work stress' but accepts help.
